article.headline: Scores from last Night: Ripley ends West Union’s perfect start; South Pontotoc reaches 8–0
article.html:
Ripley handed West Union its first reported boys basketball loss Tuesday, while Lawrence County edged Brookhaven by a point to end another perfect start. South Pontotoc’s girls stayed unbeaten, beating Mooreville to reach a listed 8–0 in one of the day’s notable North Mississippi results.

Pontotoc won comfortably in both basketball divisions, and Booneville protected unbeaten records for its girls and boys. These are selected verified varsity finals from November 24, 2026, with postgame records as listed on the completed matchup reports. They follow the matchups highlighted in our Tuesday Games To Watch preview.

Ripley stops West Union’s unbeaten start

Ripley beat West Union 63–45, moving the Tigers to a listed 5–1 and leaving the Eagles at 7–1. The result ended West Union’s loss-free opening and gave Ripley a win over a team that had yet to lose.

Lawrence County wins a one-point game against Brookhaven

Lawrence County edged Brookhaven 46–45. The Cougars are listed at 7–2 after the victory, while Brookhaven is 6–1 after its first reported defeat. A single point separated teams that both came into the meeting with several wins, turning one of Tuesday’s stronger record-based matchups into one of its closest verified finals.

South Pontotoc girls reach 8–0; Mooreville wins the boys game

South Pontotoc’s girls beat Mooreville 60–51 and are listed at 8–0. The Troopers are 5–4. The Cougars protected their perfect start against an opponent with a winning record, keeping their opening record free of defeats.

Mooreville won the boys matchup 47–20. The Troopers are listed at 6–3 and South Pontotoc at 4–4. The schools therefore split the reported varsity results, with the Cougars’ girls preserving an unbeaten opening and Mooreville’s boys improving their winning record.

Pontotoc wins in both divisions

Pontotoc’s boys defeated Baldwyn 73–41 and are listed at 5–1. The Bearcats are 1–1. The Warriors’ winning start continued with a wide final margin, giving them another victory in their strong early start.

The Pontotoc girls beat Center Hill 66–7. The Warriors are also listed at 5–1, while the Mustangs are 3–4. Both Pontotoc teams finished their reported Tuesday games with comfortable wins; the girls allowed just seven points in the completed game.

Booneville keeps both basketball records perfect

Booneville’s girls beat Starkville 43–37 to reach a listed 4–0. Starkville is 5–2. The Blue Devils protected their unbeaten record against another winning team in a game decided by a narrow final margin.

The Booneville boys won 77–56 against Grenada and are listed at 3–0; the Chargers are 2–5. For Booneville, the two results extended successful openings in both divisions.

Hancock, East Union and Gulfport stay unbeaten

Hancock’s girls beat Northeast Jones 68–46 and remain perfect at a listed 8–0. The Tigers are 4–5. East Union’s girls also kept a loss-free record, defeating Belmont 63–50 to reach 6–0. Belmont is 2–4 after the game.

Gulfport’s boys defeated Wayne County 64–46. The Admirals are listed at 5–0 and the War Eagles at 1–4. Gulfport joined Booneville and Potts Camp among the boys teams that protected unbeaten records in these verified finals.

Kossuth sweeps McNairy Central

Kossuth’s girls beat McNairy Central 67–56, improving to a listed 4–2. McNairy Central is 3–1 after its first reported loss. The Aggies stopped the visitors’ unbeaten start while strengthening a winning record of their own.

Kossuth won the boys game 70–56, leaving the Aggies listed at 3–1 and McNairy Central at 2–2. Both Kossuth teams finished ahead of the same opponent, with the boys and girls each adding to a winning opening record.

Corinth girls win again; Alcorn Central closes at an even record

Corinth’s girls beat Tunica Academy 62–27 and are listed at 6–1. Tunica Academy is 1–1. The Warriors added another decisive result to an opening in which they have lost only once.

Alcorn Central’s boys beat Itawamba Agricultural 51–44 and are listed at 3–3; the Indians are 2–5. The Golden Bears won the first quarter 16–11 and the second 15–13. Itawamba took the third 12–10, but Central won the fourth 10–8 to finish ahead. Those closing points preserved the advantage built before halftime.

Walnut wins twice; Falkner girls beat Jumpertown

Walnut’s girls beat Lafayette 61–26 and are listed at 8–2. The Wildcats’ boys defeated Jumpertown 64–51 and are 6–1. Walnut outscored Jumpertown 20–9 in the second quarter and 15–11 in the fourth; the Cardinals are listed at 4–4 after the loss.

Falkner’s girls defeated Jumpertown 58–19. The Eagles are listed at 4–3, while the Cardinals are 0–8. Falkner won every quarter, including a 20–7 opening period and a 17–4 second, building the early advantage that shaped the final.

Potts Camp’s boys beat Falkner 72–9 and remain unbeaten at a listed 7–0. The Eagles are 0–6. Potts Camp opened with a 35–1 first quarter and held Falkner scoreless in the second and fourth. The Cardinals’ perfect start continued with another large-margin result.

Hickory Flat’s boys edged Hatley 67–63. The Rebels are listed at 5–5 and the Tigers at 1–5. Hickory Flat finished on the winning side of a much closer final than the other reported area boys games in this section.

Oxford sweeps Bayou; DeSoto Central wins with a strong second half

Oxford’s girls beat Bayou Academy 62–28 and are listed at 7–1. The Charger boys won 73–49 against Bayou and are 2–2. Bayou’s corresponding records are 3–7 for the girls and 2–4 for the boys. The sweep gave both Oxford teams a win in the reported Tuesday games.

DeSoto Central’s boys defeated Independence 65–45 and are listed at 4–2, with the Wildcats at 4–5. The Jaguars took the third quarter 21–10 and the fourth 20–14. Those two periods opened the separation after Independence had won the second quarter 9–7.

Hernando’s boys beat Senatobia 65–58 to reach a listed 8–1; Senatobia is 0–3. Lewisburg defeated Ashland 91–49, leaving the Patriots at 4–3 and the Blue Devils at 1–9.

Ingomar wins by one; Tupelo and Ocean Springs add victories

Ingomar’s girls edged Jackson Prep 38–37. The Falcons are listed at 9–1 and the Patriots at 6–3. Tupelo’s girls won another close game, beating Our Lady Academy 57–53 to move to 2–3; the Crescents are 5–4.

Ocean Springs’ boys beat Gulf Shores, Alabama, 69–45 and are listed at 8–1. D’Iberville’s girls won 44–5 against Long Beach, with the Warriors listed at 1–7 and the Bearcats at 0–6. For the preceding night’s results and context, see our Monday varsity recap.
